Theme

magic noun

also magical, witchcraft, sorcery, spell, magic spell, by magic, magician, wizard

classical

Verg. A. 4.493: magicās … artēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. magicus)
Traupman 167

ars magica, artis magicae f.

magic, the magic arts

Usually plural, artēs magicae; magicus is poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). A magician is magus, a witch maga or saga.

Other words

  • venēficium, venēficiī n. — sorcery, a spell; poisoning

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 217: venēficiīs et cantiōnibus Titiniae (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 18.43

    Its first sense is poisoning; then the brewing of magic potions and spells. Black magic rather than a conjuror’s tricks (see magic trick).

  • magīa, magīae f. — magic, sorcery

    noun, first declension · also used · post-classical · Apul. Met. 3.16 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. magic (paranormal or supernatural)

    Greek; Apuleius’s word in his defence against a charge of magic, and Prudentius’s.

  • cantiō, cantiōnis f. — a spell, an incantation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 160: hāc cantiōne sānum fīet

    A song, and so a sung charm; also carmen (carmina magica).

Examples

  • venēficia mea, Quirītēs, haec sunt

    these, citizens, are my magic spellsPlin. NH 18.43

  • luxum sīquod est, hāc cantiōne sānum fīet

    if anything is out of joint, it will be healed with this spellCato Agr. 160

See also magic trick.
